How updates work

Every change is logged.

Guidance goes out of date when a process changes and nobody says so. From V.02, every course shows who owns it, its version, and the date it was last updated, and every change is listed on the course and on this page.

  • Each course has a Course record at the bottom: owner, version, review status, and what changed.
  • Pay-impacting courses carry a Before you submit block: what to attach, what to check, the cutoff, and who does what.
  • Anything not yet confirmed is marked To confirm or listed as an open item, so nobody mistakes a draft for a rule.

To confirmWho tells HCMs when a pay-impacting course changes, how the notice is sent, and how often each course is reviewed.

Nov 13, 2026 · V.02 draft

Owners are teams.

Each course is owned by a team. The owner shows at the top of the course, on its job aid, and in its Course record.

  • Payroll owns all payroll and financial topics: 20 courses.
  • HRIS owns everything else, from recruiting and hiring through assignment changes, offboarding, leave, records and reporting, and the foundations: 48 courses.

The draft first showed the owners as Payroll and Finance and as Recruiting and Hiring, and 30 courses had no owner. Every course now has one.

From Vanderbilt's published pages

These facts were read from the HR/Payroll Calendar for 2026 and 2027 and from the Vanderbilt Student Privacy Statement. They replace guesses and close open items.

  • The Shared Administrative Calendar now follows the published calendar: where it is, each cutoff, and when time cards are due.
  • Monthly cutoff: the 18th in most months and earlier in December. Courses that said the 15th to the 18th are corrected.
  • Time cards: due at noon on the Monday after the pay period ends. Holiday weeks move it.
  • Off-cycle runs: about two a month, with a cutoff of noon two days before.
  • FERPA: Vanderbilt's directory information list, and the University Registrar as the contact.

To confirmThe 2027 calendar adds a Semi Monthly payroll that no course covers yet, and the Retro Change Cutoff used by the costing courses is not on the published calendar.

Nov 12, 2026 · V.02 draft

Getting pay right the first time.

These changes add standard documents and checks, clearer ownership, cutoffs, the time card approval rule, and pay rules to the courses. All of it is a draft for the owners to confirm.

New courses (5)

  • What to attach: documents by transaction
  • Who owns what: your part, by transaction
  • Pay rules: overtime, holidays, shifts, and on-call
  • Common pay errors and how to avoid them
  • The Shared Administrative Calendar

Before you submit added (24)

  • Create a position
  • Update a position
  • Create a requisition
  • Convert a pending worker
  • Change Assignment
  • Change Working Hours
  • Transfer or promotion without a requisition
  • Review and approve time cards
  • Enter PTO for an employee
  • Request an off-cycle payment
  • Change salary
  • Process grossed-up additional compensation
  • Add a one-time payment (such as a sign-on bonus)
  • Add a staff supplement
  • Voluntary termination
  • Reduction in force (RIF)
  • Involuntary termination (misconduct)
  • Enter costing for a person
  • Change existing costing
  • Add Assignment
  • Promote
  • How to handle a termination when an employee has multiple assignments
  • Entering and managing FMLA/TMLA transactions (continuous vs. intermittent)
  • Student and faculty assignment changes

Time card approval rule added (3)

  • Weekly time card check
  • Review and approve time cards
  • UKG: Timecards, Time Off, and Schedules for Managers

On every course (68)

  • Owner, version, and updated date at the top, and a Course record with the change log at the bottom.

Assessment

  • Four questions added to the final assessment: time card approval, a change still pending at the cutoff, your part in a pay error, and what to attach.
